feedback.details: Diagram passes mmdc validation (exit 0) with exactly 5 Container nodes (mobile, web, qr_scanner, photo_capture, hermes) and all edges use explicit typing (-->, <-->). However, the diagram title appears twice: once in YAML frontmatter (line 2) and again inside the Mermaid code block (line 89). Container node qr_scanner and photo_capture use tech labels '(Docker, Native Camera)' which are internally contradictory — Docker containers cannot expose 'Native Camera' APIs (they are device-level browser/mobile APIs). This architectural mislabeling of tech stack should reduce the score slightly. All edges are explicitly typed with '-->' or '<-->', meeting the contract requirement.

All 5 required containers are present as distinct nodes: Mobile App Frontend (line 20), Web Interface (line 24), QR Scanner (line 28), Photo Capture (line 32), Hermes Agent (line 36). Each has a one-sentence responsibility description and matches PRD terminology. However, the tech labels inside the diagram nodes are architecturally inconsistent: qr_scanner and photo_capture are labeled '(Docker, Native Camera)' (lines 98-99) — Docker containers cannot host native camera APIs, which are device/browser-level. The Web Interface is labeled '(Next.js, React)' (line 97) while Mobile App is '(React Native)' (line 96), which is internally contradictory since both serve the same frontend purpose with different tech stacks.

The narrative maps containers to FR/NFR IDs but with critical gaps. Mobile App Frontend (line 22) cites 'FR41-FR45' ✓ and Web Interface (line 26) cites 'FR41-FR45' ✓. However, QR Scanner (line 30) maps to 'FR2, FR5, FR12, FR43' — only FR43 is within the required FR41-FR45 set. Photo Capture (line 34) maps to 'FR9, FR43' — only FR43 is in range. Hermes Agent (line 38) maps to 'FR13-FR40' — none are in FR41-FR45. The contract requires each of the 5 containers to link to at least one FR41-FR45 ID. Three of five containers fail this requirement. Furthermore, the narrative claims on lines 22 and 26 state that both Mobile App and Web Interface provide 'plant data entry, QR scanning, photo capture, and Hermes agent interaction' — identical descriptions for two different containers, which is vague and provides no differentiating responsibility. No NFRs are explicitly mapped per-container in the Container Definitions section; NFR references only appear in the edge case sections.

Multiple out-of-scope or hallucinated components detected. (1) The QR Scanner and Photo Capture containers are labeled with '(Docker, Native Camera)' technology (lines 98-99), which is architecturally impossible — Docker containers cannot expose native camera APIs. These are device/browser capabilities, not Docker services. This constitutes hallucinated infrastructure. (2) The Web Interface (line 24-26) is described identically to the Mobile App Frontend, providing the same capabilities — this may be scope creep if the PRD defines a single frontend surface. (3) The relationship on line 46 describes 'Mobile App Frontend ↔ Web Interface via HTTPS/REST' — two frontend clients communicating directly via REST is unusual architecture and potentially out-of-scope. (4) Line 62 contains a trailing space (MD009 violation). (5) Line 89 contains a duplicate 'title:' in the Mermaid code block. Post-MVP items are not explicitly tagged per the contract requirement.

The relationship table (lines 42-52) and diagram edges (lines 104-118) have multiple protocol deficiencies. (1) Lines 44-45: Gardener→Mobile and Gardener→Web use 'Direct human interaction' as protocol — not a network protocol, and correctly so for actor relationships, but the table treats this as a system-to-system row. (2) Lines 47, 50: 'Native camera API' and 'Browser Media API getUserMedia' are API surface names, not transport protocols. The contract requires exact protocol (HTTPS/MQTT/BLE/HTTP). (3) Lines 46: Mobile App↔Web Interface via 'HTTPS/REST' with 'JSON' payload and 'Bearer token' auth — two frontend clients should not communicate directly via REST. (4) Lines 49, 52: Hermes uses 'HTTPS/Telegram Bot API' with 'JSON message objects' and 'Bot token in Authorization header' — the Telegram Bot API typically uses long-polling or webhooks, not direct HTTP with Bearer tokens; the auth method description is vague. (5) In the diagram edges (lines 107-118), the edge labels cram protocol, payload, and auth into a single string (e.g., 'HTTPS/Telegram Bot API JSON message objects Bot token'), making it impossible to independently verify each required field.

Fails multiple mandatory lint rules with numerous violations: (1) MD013 (line-length): 19 violations found — lines 9, 15, 22, 26, 30, 38, 42, 44-52, 58, 62, 64, 66, 67, 76, 82-83 exceed 80 characters. Line 9 is 284 chars, line 58 is 262 chars. The requirement specifies 'zero errors' on MD013. (2) MD025 (single-title/single-h1): 1 error at line 5 — there are multiple top-level headings. The YAML frontmatter title and the H1 '# Plant Tracking System - C2 Container Diagram' both count as titles. (3) MD060 (table-column-style): multiple errors at lines 49-52 where table pipes do not align. (4) MD009 (trailing-spaces): line 67 has a trailing space. (5) MD047 (single-trailing-newline): line 119 missing final newline. The document uses fenced code blocks with 'mermaid' language tags (lines 87, 88) which is correct.

Completely fails this criterion. The document states at line 58: 'Out of scope for MVP... No local storage schema, queue capacity, conflict resolution, or sync backoff is implemented in MVP.' The contract explicitly requires: (1) local storage schema (IndexedDB/SQLite) — NOT provided. (2) Queue capacity limits — NOT provided. (3) Conflict resolution strategy (LWW vs manual merge) — NOT provided. (4) Explicit timeout thresholds — NOT provided. (5) Data eviction policies — NOT provided. (6) Sync backoff — NOT provided. Simply declaring something 'out of scope' when the sprint contract mandates these details is a contract rejection. Additionally, line 13 states 'Offline mode is not required (PRD: Technical Architecture Considerations)' which directly contradicts the requirement. The C1 context diagram (c2-container.md, line 23) mentions 'offline data queuing with synchronization upon reconnection' as part of failure handling, creating a cross-document inconsistency.

This section is reasonably detailed but has minor gaps. (1) Fallback UI states defined: 'Degraded' (dimmed button with tooltip) and 'Offline' (banner message) at line 62 — adequate. (2) Data staleness tolerance: '>24h flagged with warning, >72h triggers refresh' at line 63 — meets the >24h requirement. (3) User notification mechanism: 'Toast notifications for state changes, Telegram notifications for critical failures' at line 64 — specified. (4) Error boundaries: 'React error boundaries isolating Hermes UI components' at line 65 — specified. (5) Retry backoff: 'Exponential (5s, 10s, 20s, 40s) capped at 5 minutes with HTTP 429 respect' at line 66 — the cap at 5 minutes matches the contract, but the sequence sums to only 75s total, and 'capped at 5 minutes' is ambiguous (is it the total cap or max single delay?). (6) Graceful degradation paths listed for Mobile App and Web Interface at lines 68-69, but the description 'shows cached data if available' is vague — no specification of what data is cached or how long it persists. (7) The 'Hermes Agent: N/A (agent itself is the service)' at line 70 is a tautology, not a degradation path. (8) Telegram notifications at line 64 assume Telegram connectivity, which may be unavailable during degradation.

The document provides partial coverage but fails key requirements. (1) Data at rest: 'AES-256-GCM encryption' at line 74 — this is appropriate. However, the PRD reference 'PRD: Reliability' is vague — the contract requires referencing PRD security constraints verbatim. (2) Data in transit: 'TLS 1.2+' at line 75 — the contract requires 'TLS 1.2+', this meets it. Again, the PRD reference is imprecise. (3) Plaintext logging prohibition: 'No full QR payloads, image metadata, or observation details logged' at line 76 — adequate but the PRD reference 'PRD: Reliability implies data integrity' is not a security constraint citation. (4) No mention of key management for AES-256-GCM. (5) No mention of PII handling procedures beyond the general logging prohibition. (6) The contract requires 'Must reference PRD security constraints verbatim' — no verbatim PRD security sections are quoted. (7) No specification of encryption key storage location (e.g., OS keychain, hardware-backed keystore).

This section covers the required metrics with reasonable detail. (1) Render time: '<200ms initial paint, <50ms interaction to frame' at line 80 — meets the <200ms and <50ms thresholds specified in the contract. (2) Memory limits: '150MB mobile, 100MB web JS heap' at line 81 — specific values provided. (3) GC considerations: 'Object pools for QR/photo buffers, incremental GC for logs, web workers for image processing' at line 82 — specific mitigation strategies. (4) Mitigation strategies at line 83: 'Lazy loading, request queuing with priority, Hermes debouncing at 500ms' — adequate. However, (5) No explicit mention of per-container render time budgets — the thresholds are stated globally rather than per-container. (6) The '<50ms interaction to frame' is unusually specific ('to frame') but not clearly tied to a specific PRD section.

overall_summary: The C2 Container document for Sprint 3 (Frontend Container) passes Mermaid syntax validation and includes all 5 required container nodes, but suffers from critical failures in multiple contract-critical areas. The Offline Queue & Sync criterion is completely failed (score 1.0): the document declares it 'out of scope for MVP' when the sprint contract explicitly requires detailed specifications. This is a fundamental contract rejection. The Narrative Quality & Mapping criterion fails because 3 of 5 containers (QR Scanner, Photo Capture, Hermes Agent) lack mappings to FR41-FR45 as required. Markdown linting produces 19+ MD013 violations, 1 MD025 violation, plus MD009 and MD047 errors — zero tolerance was required. Relationship Documentation suffers from vague protocol descriptions ('Native camera API', 'Direct human interaction') and a suspicious Mobile App↔Web Interface REST relationship. PRD Scope Accuracy is compromised by Docker-labeled containers that cannot expose native camera APIs. The Hermes Degradation and Data Privacy sections are partially adequate but lack verbatim PRD security citations and complete technical detail.
